benefits.titleEn: It describes more than simply joining
benefits.en: The company jumped on the bandwagon.
benefits.zh: 你可以用一個簡潔的慣用語，同時表達「較遲加入」、「受到成功吸引」及「模仿潮流」等意思。

benefits.en: unoriginal; opportunistic; influenced by popularity; insufficiently independent; commercially motivated.
benefits.zh: 這個表達可以顯示說話者認為某項決定缺乏原創性、帶有投機成分、受到人氣影響，或主要由商業利益推動。

benefits.titleEn: It is useful when discussing trends
benefits.en: fashion; social media; business strategies; new technology; entertainment; food trends; public campaigns; popular opinions.
benefits.zh: 這個表達特別適合討論時裝、社交媒體、商業策略、新科技、娛樂、飲食潮流、公眾運動及熱門意見。

benefits.titleEn: It can warn against blind conformity
benefits.titleZh: 在了解風險前，不要盲目跟風
benefits.en: Do not jump on the bandwagon until you understand the risks. The expression can encourage independent thought rather than automatic imitation.
benefits.zh: 在了解風險前，不要盲目跟風。 這個表達可以鼓勵人獨立思考，而不是自動模仿其他人。

benefits.titleZh: 我抗拒了幾個月，但最後還是跟上潮流，開始觀看這套劇集
benefits.en: I resisted for months, but I have finally jumped on the bandwagon and started watching the series. The speaker can acknowledge their own late participation without seriously criticising themselves.
benefits.zh: 我抗拒了幾個月，但最後還是跟上潮流，開始觀看這套劇集。 說話者可以輕鬆承認自己較遲才加入流行活動，而不一定是在嚴厲批評自己。

benefits.titleEn: It helps learners understand authentic commentary
benefits.en: The expression frequently appears when people discuss why companies, politicians, consumers or media organisations suddenly support a successful trend.
benefits.zh: 這個表達常見於人們討論公司、政治人物、消費者或傳媒機構為何突然支持某項成功潮流的情境。

benefits.titleEn: It should not replace every form of join or follow
benefits.en: Use jump on the bandwagon only when the popularity or success of others has meaningfully influenced the decision.
benefits.zh: 只有當一項事物的人氣或他人的成功確實影響了加入決定時，才適合使用 jump on the bandwagon。

origin.statusZh: 原檔沒有另列來源可信度

history.en: A bandwagon was originally a large wagon that carried a musical band in a circus procession. The word is recorded in American English from the nineteenth century. Such wagons later appeared in political campaign celebrations and public rallies, where supporting a successful candidate could be imagined as getting onto the candidate’s moving wagon.
history.zh: 原本是馬戲團巡遊中運載樂隊的大型車輛。 這個詞在十九世紀的美式英語中已有記錄。 這類載有樂隊的車輛後來也出現在政治競選活動和公眾集會中，因此，支持一名聲勢日益強勁的候選人便可以被想像成登上對方正在前進的車輛。

history.en: P. T. Barnum used the literal term band wagon in his 1855 autobiography, but the evidence does not show that he personally invented the later figurative idiom. The figurative political sense of attaching oneself to something likely to succeed is recorded by 1899 in the writings of Theodore Roosevelt.
history.zh: 在1855年的自傳中曾使用字面的 band wagon，但現有證據並不能證明後來的比喻慣用語由他本人創造。 到了1899年，Theodore Roosevelt 的文章中已有相關比喻用法，表示加入一項看來即將成功的事物。

origin.memoryEn: Use the source meaning and examples as the memory link.
origin.memoryZh: 以原檔的核心意思及例句作為記憶提示。

rules.en: Although onto may be possible in a completely literal sentence involving physical movement, the established idiom normally uses on.
rules.zh: 在這個固定慣用語中，應使用 on，而不是 in、at 或其他介詞。
在本課教授的固定表達中，bandwagon 前面必須使用 the。

rules.titleEn: The trend should already be popular or successful
rules.en: The expression normally describes joining after a trend, activity or opinion has gained popularity, support or visible success. She did not jump on the bandwagon because no existing popular trend had yet been established.
rules.zh: 這個慣用語通常形容某項潮流、活動或意見已經獲得人氣、支持或成功之後，某人才加入。 較弱的語境：

rules.titleEn: Joining is not automatically “jumping on the bandwagon”
rules.en: A person may join an activity because they genuinely believe in it, because they have carefully studied it or because it has finally become practical.; the person wanted the same advantages; the person joined late; the decision was imitative or opportunistic.
rules.zh: 某人加入一項活動，可能是因為真正認同它、仔細研究過它，或條件終於變得可行。 這些情況不一定屬於「跟風」。 語境應顯示人氣、他人的成功、潛在利益、較遲加入或模仿行為影響了決定。

rules.titleZh: 公司完成兩年安全研究後採用了這項科技
rules.en: The company adopted the technology after completing a two-year safety study. The company ignored the technology until its competitors began making large profits, and then it adopted the same approach. This context naturally supports jump on the bandwagon.
rules.zh: 公司完成兩年安全研究後採用了這項科技。 公司一直忽視這項科技，直至競爭對手開始賺取巨額利潤後，才採用相同做法。 第二個語境較自然地支持「跟風加入」的意思。

rules.en: The incorrect version changes possibility into a completed fact.
rules.zh: 如果原句表示「可能跟隨」，答案便不應改成「已經跟隨」。

rules.titleEn: Modified forms exist, but this exercise uses the exact target
rules.en: Correct target: Jump on the Bandwagon. Incorrect target forms: jump on the fitness bandwagon; jump on the artificial-intelligence bandwagon; jump on the sustainability bandwagon.
rules.zh: 英語中可以在 bandwagon 前加入特定潮流的名稱。 不過，本練習為了集中訓練固定表達，所有答案均使用完整的 jump on the bandwagon。

rules.titleEn: Related variants are excluded from this exercise
rules.en: These may be natural in some contexts, but they are not the target answers in this set.
rules.zh: 相關形式在某些語境中可以成立，但本練習只接受 jump on the bandwagon。
